description:
Issue summary: After a scheduled optimizer experiment ramp (aggressive batching + PTQ quant profile) for tenant MapleAI, some long-lived streaming sessions saw sustained p95 latency spikes and occasional 5xx stream disconnects. An automated rewind script was run to restore the previous optimizer profile but the script returned success while the serving runtime continued to use the new profile for in-flight sessions. Impact: customer 95th percentile latency doubled on several routes; several high-value customers reported streaming disconnects during video ingestion workflows. Risk of SLA breach.

Environment: production, dedicated pool (MapleAI-reserved), us-west-2, runtime version rw-runtime@2026.03.01, optimizer-config v3.5.

Requested outcome: restore pre-experiment optimizer profile for both new and existing streaming sessions (or gracefully drain affected sessions) and provide a reproducible fix for the rewind script so it truly reconciles in-flight session config state.
steps_to_reproduce: 1) In dedicated pool with tenant pin to optimizer-config v3.5, create a long-lived streaming session (>60s) that uses async incremental batching and prefix KV caching.
2) Trigger an optimizer feature ramp: enable aggressive-batching and ptq-evict-heuristics via feature flag for that tenant.
3) Observe p50/p95 latency baseline for streaming routes for ~10m, then initiate the automated rewind script that toggles optimizer profile back to v3.4 snapshot.

4) Note that API indicates script completed successfully, but in-flight streaming sessions still observe increased p95 and occasional stream disconnects; new sessions may or may not pick up the older profile depending on worker reuse.
logs_and_observations: runtime logs: rw-runtime WARN optimizer: attempted profile revert for tenant=mapleai tenant_snapshot=v3.4 returned success but session router did not evict worker cache (worker-id=gw-12f4)
scheduler logs: scheduler INFO drain: initiated drain for worker gw-12f4 but drain timed out after 120s while sessions remained active
console metrics: p95 for /v1/stream/generate increased from 210ms -> 520ms between 2026-03-10T14:02Z and 2026-03-10T14:12Z
customer telemetry: MapleAI ingest pipeline reported 2.1% stream disconnect rate during the window
temporary_mitigation: Scoped traffic split: moved MapleAI traffic to a fallback routing policy that targets a compatible non-experimental model variant (rw-optimized/8b-compat) and throttled aggressive-batching flag for that tenant. This reduced p95 to ~280ms for most routes while we investigate.
investigation_notes:
Initial hypothesis: the rewind script updated tenant config in control plane but did not force worker-side KV eviction for in-flight sessions. Worker reuse and persistent KV caches mean sessions continued using PTQ-compiled kernels. Evidence: worker process gw-12f4 retained kv_cache_hits and used quantized kernel paths after revert. Repro on staging by running revert without explicit 'session-evict' call reproduces behaviour.

Next steps: add explicit worker eviction step to revert script, validate idempotent session drain procedure, add reconciliation check that queries worker process for active optimizer profile. Confirm changes in staging with long-lived sessions before prod redeploy.
actions_taken: 1) Applied emergency traffic split to fallback model variant for MapleAI (completed 2026-03-10T15:04Z).
2) Manually forced a graceful drain on 3 workers showing inconsistent optimizer state (gw-12f4, gw-18a9, gw-2d7c).
3) Rolled back the revert script in control plane to block further automatic rewinds until fix is merged.
4) Captured detailed worker debug traces and uploaded to internal S3 for analysis (link: s3://redwood-debug/mapleai/rewind-2026-03-10.tar.gz).
comments: Aisha Malik (Support): Noted customer escalation at 2026-03-10T14:20Z; applied traffic split and escalated to SRE for worker eviction guidance.
SRE (Diego Ramos): Confirmed worker-level KV cache persisted after control-plane revert. Proposed adding 'force-evict-sessions' and 'reconcile-worker-config' steps to revert script.
Customer (MapleAI - Priya Singh): Reported downstream ingest back to normal after traffic split but asked for permanent fix and explanatory postmortem.
Eng (Runtime Team - Mei Chen): Will prepare PR to add worker reconciliation check and make revert script atomic and idempotent. Targeting patch in staging by 2026-03-12.
Diego Ramos: Created temporary runbook snippet to drain workers safely when rolling back optimizer profile; included timeouts and metrics to watch.
proposed_fix: Patch revert script to perform three-phase revert: (1) update tenant control-plane config, (2) query active workers and force-evict or gracefully drain sessions tied to old optimizer state, (3) verify worker reports new profile before allowing new sessions. Add a safe fallback that routes traffic away if drain does not complete within configured window. Add automated test that runs a long-lived streaming session in staging and validates profile reconciliation.
resolution: In progress: Runtime PR #1428 implements worker reconciliation and forced-evict API. After successful staging validation (long-lived streams test passed), we will schedule a controlled rollout. Temporary mitigations restored service levels while fix is validated. Final resolution will include a customer-facing postmortem and the updated revert script deployed to prod.
follow_up_items: 1) Deploy PR #1428 to staging and run long-lived streaming regression suite (owner: Mei Chen, due: 2026-03-12).
2) Add unit & integration tests for revert script (owner: Runtime Tools, due: 2026-03-14).
3) Draft customer postmortem and share timelines with MapleAI CS contact (owner: Aisha Malik, due: 2026-03-15).
4) Update Confluence runbook with new forced-evict procedure and safe timeouts (owner: SRE Docs, due: 2026-03-16).
